title: Sherlock debuglet and runbook translator for reproducible admin tasks
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem: On-call engineers repeatedly re-create context (logs, live KV cache snippets, model metadata) to run runbook steps; ad-hoc scripts lead to variability and unsafe live fixes.

Goal: Build a lightweight "Sherlock" debuglet that captures a compact, replayable snapshot of the runtime context for an admin incident and a runbook translator that converts prose runbook steps into typed tasklets suitable for automated dry-run and permission-gated replay. The feature should enable safe rehearsal, improve reproducibility of fixes, and surface telemetry for post-incident analysis.

Scope: MVP includes: 1) debuglet binary that captures process state (selected logs, request trace IDs, KV cache keys, model/version metadata) into an immutable artifact; 2) a translator service that parses curated runbook markdown (Confluence/Drive) to produce a typed tasklet manifest (inputs, outputs, permission level, estimated risk); 3) a dry-run harness in the admin console to replay tasklets against captured snapshot with no external side-effects; 4) telemetry events for each tasklet execution and a simple acceptance gating policy (requires approver for high-risk tasks).

Non-goals: full natural-language-to-action synthesis, cross-region snapshot federation, or replacing existing runbook DSLs in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Sherlock debuglet can capture and upload a 10-50MB snapshot artifact to the internal ops store and provide a stable artifact ID.
Runbook translator converts three canonical runbook formats into typed tasklets with >=90% fidelity on a 20-case test corpus maintained in Drive.
Dry-run harness can execute read-only tasklets against a snapshot and flag any side-effect attempts; end-to-end smoke test recorded in CI.
Permission gating enforced: high-risk tasklets require explicit approver; policy is configurable via console feature flag.
Telemetry emitted for capture, translation, dry-run, and live-execution with tokens to correlate to incident IDs in the postmortem dashboard.
Documentation and runbook for operators: Confluence design doc, quickstart (1 page), and example PR in repo with tests.
comments: 2025-02-14 Marcus Chen: Created ticket after post-incident review; current manual debugging steps took 45m and produced two divergent fixes. Goal set to reduce mean-time-to-fix and improve reproducibility.

2025-02-16 Design sync: Decided to restrict snapshot contents to non-sensitive metadata by default; PII must be redacted via a redact-list in config. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Sherlock+debuglet+design

2025-02-17 Engineering note (Sofia): Prototyped a debuglet that serializes selected /proc and application tracing context; initial artifact produced (sherlock-20250217-0001.tar.gz) and uploaded to ops-store. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427

2025-02-18 Security review (Ana Ruiz): Redaction approach acceptable; recommend adding KMS encryption for snapshots in private deployments and an allowlist for sensitive keys. Follow-up: add KMS integration ticket if enabling for Private customers.

2025-02-19 Code review feedback (Liam O'Connor): Translator should produce explicit permission-level metadata and include a unique stable tasklet id for replayability. Marked TODO to add deterministic hashing of tasklet manifests.

2025-02-20 Sofia Martinez: Implemented dry-run harness stub in console and added telemetry hooks; QA will run replay scenarios against three incident snapshots next week. Recorded demo: drive.google.com/example-demo
